pr_title: pgwire: ignore all messages after extended protocol error
pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/103936

The protocol says:
> When an error is detected while processing any extended-query message,
> the backend issues ErrorResponse, then reads and discards messages until
> a Sync is reached, then issues ReadyForQuery and returns to normal message
> processing.

But we were implementing this incorrectly, since we should also ignore the implicit Sync that we create after processing a simple query.

Release note (bug fix): Fixed a pgwire protocol bug where CockroachDB would not ignore the messages that it should if there was an error while in the pgwire extended protocol.

issue_context.title: pgwire: should not send ReadyForQuery if there's a simple query in extended protocol error state
comments:
I saw this test when I was investigating which made me double check the protocol documentation, but you rightly called out section in at the bottom.

```
When an error is detected while processing any extended-query message, the backend issues ErrorResponse, then reads and discards messages until a Sync is reached, then issues ReadyForQuery and returns to normal message processing. (But note that no skipping occurs if an error is detected while processing Sync — this ensures that there is one and only one ReadyForQuery sent for each Sync.)
```

Maybe that only refers to executing many extended-query messages?

I think I see now - the behavior of ignoring everything until you see Sync should only be used if the error occurs during Parse, Describe, Bind, or Execute. 

Previously, I was thinking that the behavior should occur if there was an error any time before Sync was processed and after Parse, Describe, Bind, or Execute was processed.

review_comments: no relevant to your change but wondering why `if len(qargs) == 0 ` can be used determine if it's the last and only statement in the batch. Isn't it just checking if there're any arguments or placeholders?

good question! the internal executor sits in a weird place where it needs to craft these pgwire messages itself. len(qargs) is used to determine if it should use the simple protocol or the extended protocol. (the extended protocol is essentially synonymous with using a prepared statement with placeholders.)

we know it's the last in the batch because the internal executor always sends just one query per batch.
